notes:
SUMMARY: PoC started 2025-11-01 to replace incumbent (AtlasAI). Evaluation focused on chat assistant + tool-calling flows that populate downstream transaction records (structured JSON). Outcome: customer chose incumbent due to measurable quality regressions in our PoC; closed-lost on 2026-02-20.

TIMELINE / ACTIVITIES:
- 2025-10-28: Intro call (Jordan H.). Customer higher-up: VP Product (Ethan R.), PoC owner: Sr. ML Eng (Lina Vargas). Agreed to 3-week PoC + side-by-side comparison.
- 2025-11-03: Kickoff + recorded (ff_2025-11-03_0012). Scope: chat assistant for fraud triage, tool-calls to payments ledger, structured JSON output schema (txn_record).
- 2025-11-10: Mid-PoC check-in. Early signs: Redwood model produced correct intent but tool-calling occasionally returned malformed schema (extra null fields, key name mismatches). SE (Priya) proposed schema enforcement layer; customer wanted native model reliability.
- 2025-11-24: PoC results deck shared (drive:/decks/SiennaOrbit_Redwood_PoC_Results_v2.pdf). Metrics: precision on entity extraction 92% (incumbent 97%), successful tool-calls 86% (incumbent 98%). Customer highlighted downstream failures when JSON schema broken -> reconciliation errors.
- 2025-12-08: Security review submitted (drive:/security/SiennaOrbit_Security_Questions.xlsx). Security team flagged lack of HSM/KMS integration roadmap and SOC2 attestation timeline. Jira: SEC-3445 opened for HSM questions.
- 2026-01-18: Final demo + decision meeting (ff_2026-01-18_0037). Incumbent presented production logs showing consistent structured outputs and tool-call reliability; Sienna Orbit cited "better alignment w/ existing ledger adapters."
- 2026-02-02: Internal acquisition at Sienna Orbit paused budget for new infra; PoC champion (Lina V.) accepted role at competitor.
- 2026-02-15: Final outreach by AE/SE; customer confirms decision to stay with incumbent. Closed-lost noted.

CUSTOMER FEEDBACK (verbatim/paraphrase):
- "We can't afford reconciliation failures — it breaks downstream pipelines."
- "Your latency/costs were attractive, but reliability wins for us."
- "We need guaranteed HSM + SOC2 before switching for regulated flows."

ANALYSIS / PRIMARY LOSS REASONS:
- Quality regression vs incumbent: measurable gap in structured output fidelity and tool-calling correctness. Incumbent had higher-success tool-call rate and fewer schema mismatches.
- No internal champion after PoC: PoC owner left for competitor role during procurement window.
- Budget freeze: acquisition forced pause on purchasing new inference infra this quarter.
- Security blockers: immediate HSM/KMS requirement and SOC2 attestation timeline longer than customer could accept.

ACTIONS TAKEN / ITEMS TRIED:
- Schema enforcement wrapper proposal (did not meet customer's preference for model-native reliability).
- Short-term fallbacks suggested (post-processing validators + canary routing to incumbent) — customer rejected due to complexity.
- Opened SEC-3445 for prioritized HSM integration notes; engineering estimate >3 months.

LESSONS / NOTES FOR RE-ENGAGEMENT:
- For regulated fintech accounts, prioritize tool-calling reliability and deterministic structured output in onboarding benchmarks. Add end-to-end reconciliation tests in PoC (simulate downstream pipeline).
- Build quick HSM/KMS FAQ + potential timeline for SOC2 artifacts to reduce security friction in procurement.
- Track champion moves; set re-engagement triggers if champion returns or budget re-opens.

NEXT STEPS (internal):
- Jordan to run loss post-mortem w/ AE/SE/Product on 2026-03-05.
- Add targeted E2E reconciliation test to PoC template for future fintech prospects.
- Keep contact (Ethan R.) on a 3-month nurture cadence; flag if acquisition delay resolves.
